argument.text: By H001, T>0 and 0<gamma<=1. For arbitrary real mean-zero g with ||g||_{H^gamma}<=R, reflection and sign give real mean-zero -g(-x) with the same Fourier norms. In particular its L2 and dot H^gamma norms are <=R. Instantiate E001 at s=gamma, b=T, B0=R and z0=-g(-x). Thus the equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx admits a unique continuous dot H^gamma solution, and sup_{[0,T]}||U(t)||_{dot H^gamma}<=K_gamma(T,R,R), with K_gamma uniform over this ball. Smooth initial data belong to every positive integer Sobolev space; E001 at each such integer and uniqueness identify these regular solutions with the H^gamma solution, giving spatial smoothness. E001 at theta=0 and arbitrary two initial norms summing to at most B0 gives sup_{[0,T]}||U-Utilde||_2<=C(T,B0)||U(0)-Utilde(0)||_2.

produces.statement: For every real mean-zero g with ||g||_{H^gamma}<=R, there exists a unique C([0,T];dot H^gamma) solution of (Uflow)_t=Uflow (Uflow)_x+(Uflow)_xxx with Uflow(0,x)=-g(-x), with a finite uniform homogeneous norm bound depending only on T,gamma,R. For smooth initial g this solution is spatially smooth. For any two real mean-zero initial data in this class whose initial L2 norms sum to at most B0, their corresponding source-sign flows satisfy sup_{[0,T]}||Ufirst-Usecond||_2<=C(T,B0)||Ufirst(0)-Usecond(0)||_2.

argument.text: Define \(u(t,x)=-U(t,-x)\). Then \(u_t=-U_t\), \(u_x=U_x\), \(u_{xxx}=U_{xxx}\) at \((t,-x)\), and consequently \(u_t+u_{xxx}=uu_x\). Fourier coefficients become \(\widehat u(k)=-\widehat U(-k)\), preserving every Sobolev norm, reality and zero mean. This transforms the source equation to u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2). The norm comparison above transfers all bounds to our \(H^\gamma\) norm. Hence there is \(A(T,\gamma,R)<\infty\) such that every smooth initial datum in the stated ball satisfies \(\sup_{[0,T]}\|u(t)\|_{H^\gamma}\le A\). The same bound holds for the limiting solution: for each finite set of frequencies pass to the limit in its finite norm sum, then take the supremum over finite sets. Thus \(M\le1+A(T,\gamma,R)\) uniformly. Continuous dependence in \(L^2\) is precisely the input used in the final density passage. No change of torus length or amplitude scaling is needed. More explicitly, the physical change u(t,x)=-U(t,-x) maps initial data g to source initial data -g(-x), so preserves the whole initial-data ball. The homogeneous-to-inhomogeneous inequalities follow coefficientwise from |k|<=<k><=sqrt(2)|k| for k!=0. For a continuous limiting flow the finite-frequency sums and then their supremum give the bound at each time, with the same constant. Apply the source pair bound after this isometry; it gives the stated C(T,B0) bound. Twisting by S_{-t} differentiates away -partial_x^3 and gives v'=B_t(v,v)/2. This proves all clauses of the output, for arbitrary data in the ball.

argument.text:
Fix tau>0 and real phases alpha,beta. Also, independently, fix a nonzero integer quadruple of zero sum. Assume L1 to collect these antecedent conditions. If either phase vanishes its covariance vanishes by its definition. For the remaining phase case use the following calculation.
 Let \(h(s)=e^{-i\alpha s}-M_\tau(e^{-i\alpha s})\). Then \(\eta_\tau=\tau^{-1}\int_0^\tau h(s)e^{-i\beta s}\,ds\). The elementary bound
\(|h(s)|\le\tau^{-1}\int_0^\tau|\alpha||s-r|\,dr\le\tau|\alpha|\)
gives the linear phase estimate, also interchanging \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\). Moreover,
\[
|h(0)|+|h(\tau)|\le\tau|\alpha|,\qquad
\int_0^\tau|h'(s)|\,ds=\tau|\alpha|.
\]
Integrating \(e^{-i\beta s}\) once gives \(|\eta_\tau|\le2|\alpha/\beta|\). Interchanging the phases proves the ratio estimate.

argument.text:
For the quadruple let A=|ab|, B0=|cd| and N1>=N2>=N3>=N4 be the sorted magnitudes. The largest magnitude is at most the sum of the other three, hence N1<=3N2.
 For the required ratio majorant, if \(d\) is among the two largest frequencies, use \(\min(A/B0,B0/A)\le1\). Otherwise the largest two are among \(a,b,c\). If they are \(a,b\), then
\[
\frac1{|d|}\min(A/B0,B0/A)\le\frac{|c|}{|ab|}\le\frac1{N_3}.
\]
If they are \(a,c\) (the case \(b,c\) is identical), their ratio is between \(1/3\) and \(3\). The remaining magnitudes are \(|b|,|d|\), whose maximum is \(N_3\). Thus
\[
\frac1{|d|}\min(A/B0,B0/A)\le3\min\left\{\frac{|b|}{|d|^2},\frac1{|b|}\right\}
\le\frac3{\max(|b|,|d|)}.
\]
For the required sum majorant, consider the pairing \((a,b)\) and \((c,d)\). If the two largest magnitudes are in the same pair, the other pair has sum of magnitude at most \(2N_3\). Since \(a+b=-(c+d)\),
\[
\frac{|a+b|}{\max(A,B0)}\le\frac{2N_3}{N_1N_2}\le\frac2{N_3}.
\]
If the largest two belong to different pairs, the third largest is paired with one of them. Hence \(\max(A,B0)\ge N_2N_3\) and \(|a+b|\le2N_1\le6N_2\), giving the result. Ties can be ordered arbitrarily; the same alternatives cover them. 
This covers all placements and ties. Discharge L1 and universally quantify both independent choices to obtain the output.

argument.text:
Fix four nonnegative ell2 sequences, under temporary antecedent L1.  It suffices first to consider finitely supported sequences. Decompose into shells \(2^j\le|k|<2^{j+1}\), \(j\ge0\), set x_{r,j}(k)=x_r(k)1_{2^j<=|k|<2^(j+1)}, and write \(Xshell_{r,j}\) for the \(\ell^2\) norm of the \(r\)th sequence on the \(j\)th shell. Fix an ordering of the four shell indices \(j_1\ge j_2\ge j_3\ge j_4\). A nonzero zero-sum interaction has \(j_1-j_2\le2\). For each fixed pair of smaller-shell frequencies, the remaining sum of the two larger-shell sequences is at most their \(\ell^2\) norm product by Cauchy–Schwarz, since one sequence is a translated reflection of the other. Sum the smaller frequencies in \(\ell^1\). A shell has at most \(2^{j+1}\) integer elements, so another Cauchy–Schwarz bound gives
\[
\sum_{a+b+c+d=0}\prod_{r=1}^4 x_{r,j_r}
\le C2^{(j_3+j_4)/2}\prod_{r=1}^4 Xshell_{r,j_r}.
\]
Since \(N_3\ge2^{j_3}\), the weight leaves \(C2^{-(j_3-j_4)/2}\). For \(q=j_1-j_2\in\{0,1,2\}\), extend the nonnegative sum by dropping the upper restriction on the smaller shells. The contribution is at most
\[
C\left(\sum_{J0} Xshell_{1,J0}Xshell_{2,J0-q}\right)
\left(\sum_{\ell\ge m}2^{-(\ell-m)/2}Xshell_{3,\ell}Xshell_{4,m}\right).
\]
The first factor is bounded by Cauchy–Schwarz. Writing \(r=\ell-m\), the second is at most
\[
\sum_{r\ge0}2^{-r/2}\|Xshell_3\|_{\ell^2}\|Xshell_4\|_{\ell^2}
=\frac{\|Xshell_3\|_{\ell^2}\|Xshell_4\|_{\ell^2}}{1-2^{-1/2}}.
\]
Sum over at most 24 orderings and three offsets. For arbitrary nonnegative sequences apply the finite bound to their restrictions to \(|k|\le m\). The infinite positive sum is the supremum of these finite sums, while the norms of the restrictions are bounded by the full norms. This proves the infinite statement without exchanging conditionally convergent sums. 
Restriction to a subset only decreases the nonnegative sum. Discharge L1 to obtain the universally quantified output.

argument.text:
H001 supplies 0<gamma<=1 for the final numerical-state specialization. Independently fix lambda in [0,1], tau>0, step time t_n, and mean-zero polynomial inputs. Temporarily assume these range conditions as L1. Use the following computation with the proof's letter gamma replaced everywhere by lambda; no numerical state regularity is assumed.
 Only nonzero \(abck\) and \(p=a+b\ne0\) need consideration. Set \(k=a+b+c\), \(d=-k\), \(p=a+b\), \(A=|ab|\), \(B0=|ck|\), \(\alpha=3abp\), \(\beta=3kcp\), and write eta0=eta_tau(alpha,beta) as eta in this calculation. N002 and the first majorant in N002 give
\[
\frac{|\eta|}{|k|}\le\frac6{N_3}.
\]
For the other endpoint, observe that \(A B0=|abck|\), and use the linear phase bound in N002 and the second majorant in N002:
\[
\frac{|\eta|}{\tau|abck|}\le3\frac{|p|\min(A,B0)}{A B0}
=3\frac{|p|}{\max(A,B0)}\le\frac{18}{N_3}.
\]
Taking the geometric mean of these two bounds yields
\[
\boxed{\frac{|\eta_\tau(\alpha,\beta)|}{|k||abc|^\lambda}
\le\frac{6^{1-\lambda}18^\lambda\tau^\lambda}{N_3(a,b,c,-k)}.} 
\]



Dualize the remainder definition D014 against an \(\ell^2\) sequence and take absolute values. Apply N003 with \(x_1(a)=|a|^\lambda|\widehat f_1(a)|\) and analogously for \(x_2,x_3\); \(x_4(d)\) is the absolute value of the dual coefficient at \(-d\). Their norms are bounded by the inhomogeneous Sobolev norms and the dual norm. The factors \(e^{-it_n\Phi}\) have modulus one. The sum is bounded by C_lambda tau^(1+lambda) product_j||f_j||_{H^lambda}; deleting summands or multiplying them by scalars of modulus at most one preserves this absolute-value estimate. Polynomial approximation and the bound extend the operator to the claimed spaces. 
Here the two estimates used are directly N002 and the four-linear estimate is N003. At lambda=0 or 1 use the corresponding endpoint directly, so no 0^0 convention is needed.

produces.statement: For all lambda in [0,1], tau>0, real t_n and mean-zero polynomial f1,f2,f3, ||R^n_{2,tau}(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_lambda tau^(1+lambda) product_{j=1}^3||f_j||_{H^lambda}, with constants independent of support and time. The same estimate holds after any summand restriction or insertion of multipliers of modulus <=1. For nonzero a,b,c,k=a+b+c with p=a+b!=0, alpha=3abp and beta=3kcp, |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|/(|k||abc|^lambda)<=6^(1-lambda)18^lambda tau^lambda/N3(a,b,c,-k).

argument.text:
The polynomial estimate F001 makes each Cauchy approximation converge in L2: expand a trilinear difference into three terms and apply the same bound. It gives a unique continuous trilinear extension to the mean-zero H^lambda completions and preserves the multiplier restrictions. For the numerical-state estimate fix mean-zero w in H^gamma, f in L2, ||w||_{H^gamma}<=M, delta=||f-w||_2<=1, and 0<tau<=1.  Apply F001 at lambda=gamma with exponent \(\gamma\) to \((w,w,w)\). Expand the difference between the cubic expressions at \(f\) and at \(w\), and apply F001 at lambda=0 to every difference term. This gives \(C\tau\delta(\|f\|_{L^2}+\|w\|_{L^2})^2\). No \(H^\gamma\) bound on the numerical state is used. 
Indeed ||f||_2<=M+1, so the difference is bounded by C_M tau delta, while the value at w is <=C M^3 tau^(1+gamma). These establish both assertions. Discharge L1 and the stated conditional specialization, retaining all its conditions in the output.

argument.text: Use H001. For E002 take arbitrary I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b and b-a<=1 and lambda=0 for the X estimate. X gives precisely L-infinity L2 and L-infinity H^(-23/14) derivative, its hypotheses. Its three choices of negative-norm slot are retained. For constant inputs use E002 with any lambda in [0,1]. Each source spatial norm is sqrt(2 pi) times ours: divide by sqrt(2 pi) on the output and absorb the remaining product factors 2 pi into the constant. This proves the first two assertions without changing their exponent or time length. Smooth or continuous piecewise smooth time functions have the stated distributional derivative, so E002 applies directly. General X inputs use the source bounded interpretation of the operator. When a=b the integral is zero, so the zero-length interval case follows directly.

For time-independent fj in H^lambda and 0<=lambda<=1, ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_lambda |I|^lambda product_j||fj||_{H^lambda}; at |I|=0 the integral is zero. argument.text:
For the product and stages use E003 with lambda=gamma and epsilon=1/8 at gamma=1/2. The diagonal bilinear stage is exactly F_n(t;w), by definition. The necessary source exponent checks and retained calculations are:
when \(\|w\|_{H^\gamma}\le M\). One can take \(a_\gamma=1/2-\gamma\) for \(0<\gamma<1/2\), \(1/8\) for \(\gamma=1/2\), and \(a_\gamma=0\) for \(\gamma>1/2\). For clarity, the source stage exponent is \(\theta=(1+\gamma-\beta)/(1+\gamma-\beta_0)\), with \(\beta_0=2\gamma-3/2\) for \(0<\gamma<1/2\), \(\beta_0=-1/2-\epsilon\) for \(\gamma=1/2\), and \(\beta_0=\gamma-1\) for \(1/2<\gamma\le1\). Take \(\epsilon=1/8\) in the middle case. At \(\beta=a_\gamma\) the exponents are respectively \((1/2+2\gamma)/(5/2-\gamma)\ge\gamma\), \(11/17>1/2\) and \((1+\gamma)/2\ge\gamma\). Every \(a_\gamma\) lies in the source interval \([\beta_0,1+\gamma]\). Since \(0<\tau\le1\), these exponents imply the first bound in the asserted stage inequalities. At \(\beta=1+\gamma\) the exponent is zero, giving the second. The product inequality is E003, with the same fixed \(1/8\) choice when \(\gamma=1/2\). Source \(L^2\) and \(H^s\) norms are \(\sqrt{2\pi}\) times ours; dividing the source inequalities absorbs only fixed factors into constants. These estimates require no regularity beyond \(H^\gamma\) on \(w\). For the first range the exponent inequality reduces to gamma^2-gamma/2+1/2=(gamma-1/4)^2+7/16>0; at gamma=1/2 the exponent is 11/17 and in the last range (1+gamma)/2>=gamma. Thus both stage conclusions follow uniformly for 0<tau<=1. All relevant bounds and the product inequality have now been proved in the declared normalization.

argument.text: Fix functions in the classes stated in the output; retain those conditions as L1. Orthogonality of finite Fourier polynomials gives Parseval, hence the completion identifies H^0 with normalized L2. The multiplier exp(itk^3) has modulus one, so S_t is an isometry. Its conjugate relation at -k proves preservation of reality, and its zero coefficient proves preservation of the mean. Every Fourier projection deletes nonnegative terms of squared Sobolev sums and commutes with time derivatives, so contracts Sobolev norms and both terms of X. Comparing <k> powers on |k|<=N and |k|>N gives the two stated Bernstein inequalities, with fixed constants for N>=1. Cauchy–Schwarz gives ||Dinv f||_infinity<=(sum_{k!=0}k^(-2))^(1/2)||f||_2 and ||Dinv f||_{H^1}<=sqrt(2)||f||_2. The analogous Fourier estimate gives ||A0||_infinity<=C||A0||_{H^1}. The product rule, placing the undifferentiated factor in L-infinity in each term, gives ||A0 B0||_{H^1}<=C||A0||_{H^1}||B0||_{H^1}. Thus J_t has the asserted H^1 bound. Also ||J_t(f,g)||_2<=||S_t Dinv f||_2||S_t Dinv g||_infinity<=C||Dinv f||_2||g||_2. Density extends these products from polynomials.

produces.statement: For all real t, S_t is a Sobolev isometry preserving reality and mean, and frequency projections contract every Sobolev norm and X. For s>=s0,N>=1, ||P_{>N}f||_H^{s0}<=C N^(s0-s)||f||_H^s and ||P_{<=N}f||_H^s<=C N^(s-s0)||f||_H^{s0}. For mean-zero L2 f,g, ||Dinv f||_H^1+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_H^1<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||J_t(f,g)||_2<=C||Dinv f||_2||g||_2. For H^1 A0,B0, ||A0 B0||_H^1<=C||A0||_H^1||B0||_H^1.

argument.text: For L2 F,G the convolution coefficient bound |(FG)hat(k)|<=||F||_2||G||_2 follows by Cauchy–Schwarz. Hence ||B_t(f,g)||_{H^(-pstar)}^2<=||f||_2^2||g||_2^2 sum_{k!=0}k^2<k>^(-2pstar). This series is finite because pstar=23/14>3/2. The same coefficient bound with sum_{k!=0}k^(-2) yields ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A, <k>^(-pstar)<=|k|^(-1) for k!=0 because pstar>1, giving its claimed negative-norm inequality. All constants are independent of time by F001.

produces.statement: For mean-zero L2 f,g, ||B_t(f,g)||_H^(-pstar)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For L2 F,G, ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A with Dinv A in L2, ||A||_H^(-pstar)<=||Dinv A||_2.

argument.text: For smooth mean-zero time-dependent f,g, J_t(f,g) has coefficient sum_{a0+b0=k} exp(-3itka0b0)(ia0)^(-1)(ib0)^(-1) fhat(a0)ghat(b0) at k!=0. Differentiate: the phase derivative is 3ik times the product coefficient, so partial_t J_t(f,g)=3 B_t(f,g)+J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g'). Integrating proves the stated normal form, retaining both endpoints. The sums of smooth functions and all needed derivatives converge absolutely, justifying differentiation and integration. Symmetry is immediate from the product. Since Dinv partial_x=P, substitution gives J_t(B_t(f,g),h)=S_{-t}P{P[(S_tf)(S_tg)]S_t Dinv h}; integrate to get C_I. For a continuous piecewise smooth pair, apply on each piece; adjacent boundary values cancel, leaving both outer endpoints. No delta mass appears in its distributional derivative. Discharge L1, retaining each specified function class in its universally quantified clause.

argument.text: Assume L1: g0 is an arbitrary smooth real mean-zero datum, and let L be an arbitrary positive integer. Use the iterates initialized with g0. H001 makes tau=T/L>0. The update preserves smoothness by its products, inverse derivatives and Airy multipliers. Its first and all projected terms have mean zero; the mean of the second H_tau term vanishes because S_tau Dinv f has mean zero. Conjugate symmetry is preserved by real products, real differential operators and the Airy group, so the iterates are real. Induction establishes these properties at every grid point. E004 applied at each f=v^n gives exactly v^{n+1}=f+F_n(t_{n+1})+C_n(t_{n+1})-R2(f,f,f). In V the Q_n endpoint and its occurrence in W_n cancel. Thus V(t_n)=f and V(t_{n+1})=v^{n+1}, proving continuity between steps. Differentiating its smooth step integrals gives F_n'=B_t(f,f)/2 and V'=B_t(f+F_n,f+F_n)/2-W_n/tau. Subtract F_n' to get the claimed Y_n' and note Y_n(t_n)=0. The construction is spatially smooth and piecewise time-smooth, as claimed. Discharge L1, keeping smoothness and the real mean-zero conditions in the conditional universally quantified output.

argument.text:
Fix arbitrary smooth mean-zero f,w on the step, and assume L1: t_n>=0, 0<tau<=1, ||w||_{H^gamma}<=M and delta_n=||f-w||_2<=1. Set q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n; thus q_n<=2 and ||f||_2<=M+1. H001 fixes the exponent range. N006 gives the endpoint normal form and product bounds; N005 gives product and exact-data stage bounds; N004 gives the numerical-state cubic bound. The endpoint formula \(F_n(t)=\tfrac16[\mathcal J_s(f,f)]_{t_n}^t\) gives
\[
\sup_{I_n}\|F_n(t)\|_{H^1}\le C_M,\qquad
\sup_{I_n}\|F_n(t)-F_n(t;w)\|_{H^1}\le C_M\delta_n.
\]
Together with the stage bounds N005, this yields
\[
\sup_{I_n}\|F_n(t)\|_{H^{a_\gamma}}+\sup_{I_n}\|F_n(t)\|_{L^2}\le C_Mq_n,
\qquad\|z_n\|_{X(I_n)}\le C_M. 
\]
For the exact-data contribution, apply the product bound N005 to \(\partial_x(S_tF_n(t;w))\) and \(S_tF_n(t;w)\); use the stage bounds N005. Write \(A=F_n(t;w)\) and \(D0=F_n(t)-A\). The exact-data term obeys
\(\|\partial_x[(S_tA)^2]\|_2\le2C_\gamma\|A\|_{H^{1+\gamma}}\|A\|_{H^{a_\gamma}}\le C_M\tau^\gamma\).
The difference of squares is \((S_tD0)S_t(F_n+A)\); both second factors have bounded \(H^1\) norm and \(\|D0\|_{H^1}\le C_M\delta_n\). The \(H^1\) algebra estimate bounds its derivative by \(C_M\delta_n\). Thus
\[
\sup_{I_n}\|\mathcal B_t(F_n(t),F_n(t))\|_{L^2}\le C_Mq_n.
\]
Consequently N004 implies
\[
\sup_{I_n}\|Q_n(t)\|_{L^2}+\|W_n\|_{L^2}\le C_M\tau q_n. 
\]
These are all asserted stage and endpoint-correction bounds.

produces.statement: Uniformly on I_n, ||F_n||_H^1<=C_M, ||F_n-F_n(.;w)||_H^1<=C_M delta_n, ||F_n||_H^{a_gamma}+||F_n||_2<=C_M q_n, ||z_n||_X<=C_M, ||B_t(F_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M q_n and sup||Q_n||_2+||W_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n.

argument.text:
Differentiate the defining step integrals: F_n'=B_t(f,f)/2; expansion of B_t(f+F_n,f+F_n)/2 gives V'=B_t(z_n,z_n)/2-W_n/tau, hence Y_n'=B_t(f,F_n)+B_t(F_n,F_n)/2-W_n/tau and Y_n(t_n)=0.
To bound \(D^{-1}\mathcal B_t(f,F_n)\), use its exact expression \(S_{-t}P[(S_tf)(S_tF_n)]\). The product containing \(w\) is bounded by \(C_\gamma\|w\|_{H^\gamma}\|F_n\|_{H^{a_\gamma}}\). The product containing \(f-w\) is bounded by \(\|f-w\|_2\|S_tF_n\|_\infty\le C_M\delta_n\) using the uniform \(H^1\) bound. Therefore
\[
\sup_{I_n}\|\partial_x^{-1}\mathcal B_t(f,F_n(t))\|_{L^2}\le C_Mq_n.
\]



Use F001 and \(Y_n'=\mathcal B_t(f,F_n)+\tfrac12\mathcal B_t(F_n,F_n)-\tau^{-1}W_n\) to get
\[
\sup_{I_n}\|\partial_x^{-1}Y_n\|_{L^2}\le C_M\tau q_n,\qquad
\sup_{I_n}\|\partial_x^{-1}Y_n'\|_{L^2}\le C_Mq_n. 
\]
For the strong norm, the normal-form identity N006 and \(F_n'=\tfrac12\mathcal B_t(f,f)\) give exactly
\[
C_n(t)=\tfrac13\mathcal J_t(f,F_n(t))-\tfrac16C_{[t_n,t]}(f,f,f).
\]
The first term is \(O(q_n)\) in \(L^2\). In the second, use the constant-input trilinear bound N005 with exponent \(\gamma\) on \((w,w,w)\), and exponent zero on every term in the difference with \((f,f,f)\). Thus
\[
\sup_{I_n}\|Y_n\|_{L^2}\le C_Mq_n. 
\]
Since \(p_*>1\), the two inverse-derivative bounds just calculated imply the important pair
\[
\|Y_n\|_{X(I_n)}\le C_Mq_n,\qquad
\sup_{I_n}\|Y_n\|_{H^{-p_*}}\le C_M\tau q_n. 
\]
For the first term in the exact formula for C_n, use symmetry and the asymmetric J bound of N006 with ||F_n||_2<=C_M q_n from F001. Time-independent C_I terms use N005 on (w,w,w) at gamma and on every multilinear difference term at zero. The H^(-pstar) and derivative conclusions follow coefficientwise from Dinv and pstar>1, as in N006. This proves all clauses of the output. Discharge L1 and quantify the choices; each condition remains in the antecedent.

H001 fixes the exponent. The definition of Res concatenates increments rho_n with rho_n(t_n)=0; thus Res is continuous piecewise smooth with Res(0)=0. N007 gives V'=B_t(z_n,z_n)/2-W_n/tau. argument.text: Apply the N006 normal form to the first integral in rho_n. Since Y_n(t_n)=0, its endpoint bound is C||Dinv Y_n||_2||z_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n by N008. The derivative integral with Y_n' is <=C tau sup||Dinv Y_n'||_2 sup||z_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n. Since z_n'=B_t(f,f)/2, the other derivative term is a constant times C_[t_n,t](f,f,Y_n); N005 with negative norm on Y_n bounds it by C_M tau q_n using both ||Y_n||_X<=C_M q_n and ||Y_n||_H^(-pstar)<=C_M tau q_n. Apply N006 again to the integral with two Y_n slots. Its endpoint and derivative terms are each O(tau q_n^2), by N008, and q_n<=2 makes this O(tau q_n). The affine W_n term is <=||W_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n. This proves sup||rho_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n at every partial endpoint. Finally F001 and the B bound N006 give ||Res'||_H^(-pstar)<=C_M(q_n+q_n^2)+||W_n||_2/tau<=C_M q_n. argument.text: Use H001 and an arbitrary smooth real mean-zero datum g0 with ||g0||_{H^gamma}<=R. N001 gives its smooth exact twisted flow v and M. N007 gives continuous V agreeing with the numerical grid. Put e=v-V, I=[a,b] subset [0,T], h=b-a<=1, starting at a grid point. Assume L1: 0<tau<=1 and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1. Every intersected step has delta_n=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I. Summing the N009 increment bound over at most h/tau+1 steps gives sup_I||Res(t)-Res(a)||_2<=C_M(h+tau)(tau^gamma+E_I). The exact derivative identity is e'=B_t(e,v-e/2)-Res'. Apply N006 and N009 to get ||e||_X<=C_M(tau^gamma+E_I). Also ||V||_2<=||v||_2+1 and V'=B(V,V)/2+Res' give ||v||_X+||V||_X<=C_M. Continuity permits these statements across step interfaces.

For any \(t\in I\), define \(\mathcal F_I(t)=\int_a^t\mathcal B_s(e,v-e/2)\,ds\). The exact error identity is
\[
e(t)=e(a)+\mathcal F_I(t)-(\mathcal R(t)-\mathcal R(a)). 
\]
Choose a Fourier threshold \(N\ge2\) only in the proof. It is not part of the algorithm. The low frequencies satisfy
\[
\sup_{t\in I}\|P_{\le N}\mathcal F_I(t)\|_{L^2}\le C_MN^2hE_I. 
\]
For example \(\|\partial_x^{-1}P(fg)\|_{L^2}\lesssim\|f\|_{L^2}\|g\|_{L^2}\), followed by the two-derivative Bernstein bound, proves the low-frequency estimate.

For high frequencies, the normal-form identity N006 gives, retaining *both* endpoints,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal F_I(t)
&=\tfrac13[\mathcal J_s(e,v-e/2)]_{s=a}^{s=t}
-\tfrac13C_{[a,t]}(e,v-e/2,V)-\tfrac16C_{[a,t]}(v,v,e)\\
&\quad+\tfrac13\int_a^t\mathcal J_s(\mathcal R',V)\,ds. 
\end{aligned}
\]
For an explicit verification put \(g=v-e/2\). Then \(e'=\mathcal B(e,g)-\mathcal R'\) and \(g'=\tfrac12\mathcal B(v,v)-\tfrac12\mathcal B(e,g)+\tfrac12\mathcal R'\).
In the differentiated terms of the normal-form identity N006, symmetry of \(\mathcal J\) gives \(C(e,g,g)-\tfrac12C(e,g,e)=C(e,g,V)\) because \(g-e/2=V\).
The remaining cubic term is \(\tfrac12C(v,v,e)\), and the forcing terms are
\(-\mathcal J(\mathcal R',g)+\tfrac12\mathcal J(e,\mathcal R')=-\mathcal J(\mathcal R',V)\).
Multiplication by \(-1/3\) yields exactly the normal-form expansion. The endpoint terms after \(P_{>N}\) are bounded by \(C_MN^{-1}E_I\) by the \(H^1\) bound for \(\mathcal J\) in the elementary bounds N006.
Here P_{<=N} denotes the multiplier 1_{|k|<=N}; its complement is P_{>N}. The low estimate uses N006's Dinv P product bound and the factor k^2<=N^2. F001 gives the differentiated equations, and N006 justifies the normal form piecewise: continuous interface endpoints cancel. The initial endpoint at a is retained even when e(a)!=0.

produces.statement: With mathcal F_I(t)=integral_a^t B_s(e,v-e/2)ds, e(t)=e(a)+mathcal F_I(t)-(Res(t)-Res(a)) and sup||P_{<=N}mathcal F_I||_2<=C_M N^2 h E_I. Exactly mathcal F_I(t)=(1/3)[J_s(e,v-e/2)]_a^t-(1/3)C_[a,t](e,v-e/2,V)-(1/6)C_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Res',V)ds. The high-output boundary terms are <=C_M N^(-1)E_I.

argument.text:
We spell out how the high-output trilinear terms are estimated. If all three inputs have frequencies at most \(N/3\), the output cannot exceed \(N\). Write \(Lo=P_{\le N/3}\) and \(Hi=Id-Lo\). Here Id denotes the identity operator. The telescoping expansion is
\(C(f_1,f_2,f_3)-C(Lof_1,Lof_2,Lof_3)=C(Hif_1,f_2,f_3)+C(Lof_1,Hif_2,f_3)+C(Lof_1,Lof_2,Hif_3)\).
The low-input term has no output above \(N\), and each projection contracts both components of \(X(I)\). For the specified high input, \(\|Hif_i\|_{H^{-p_*}}\le CN^{-p_*}\|f_i\|_2\). In the time-dependent trilinear bound N005, place the \(H^{-p_*}\) norm on that input. Bernstein gives
\[
\|P_{>N}C_I(f_1,f_2,f_3)\|_{L^2}
\le Ch\prod_j\|f_j\|_{X(I)}+CN^{-p_*}\prod_j\|f_j\|_{L^\infty(I;L^2)}. 
\]
Applying F001 to the two cubic terms in the normal-form identity F002 yields \(C_Mh\tau^\gamma+C_M(h+N^{-p_*})E_I\).

The forcing integral in F002 requires the stepwise formula for \(\mathcal R'\) in the residual identity N009. On each intersected step it becomes a sum of
\[
-C(Y_n,z_n,V),\qquad-\tfrac12C(Y_n,Y_n,V),\qquad
-\tau^{-1}\int\mathcal J_s(W_n,V)\,ds.
\]
The first two are \(O(\tau q_n)\) by the time-dependent trilinear bound N005, with the negative norm on \(Y_n\), and N008, F001. The last is \(O(\tau q_n)\) by N008 and the \(L^2\) bound for \(\mathcal J\). Even for a partial final step this is a valid upper bound. Summing gives \(C_M(h+\tau)(\tau^\gamma+E_I)\). Combining these facts,
\[
\sup_{t\in I}\|P_{>N}\mathcal F_I(t)\|_{L^2}
\le C_M(h+\tau)\tau^\gamma+C_M(h+\tau+N^{-1}+N^{-p_*})E_I. 
\]
The projection names here are Lo=P_{<=N/3} and Hi=Id-Lo. By N006 they commute with time derivatives and contract X. The middle two normal-form terms each contain e once, hence their products of L2 norms contribute E_I and products of X norms contribute tau^gamma+E_I, by F001. N005 applies with any selected high input in its negative-norm slot. In the forcing integrals use the stepwise identity N009, the two Y_n norms in N008 and the bounds on V in F001. The O(tau q_n) sum includes a possible partial last step.

produces.statement: sup_{t in I}||P_{>N}mathcal F_I(t)||_2<=C_M(h+tau)tau^gamma+C_M(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))E_I, including both endpoints and the forcing contribution.

argument.text: H001 fixes T>0 and gamma>0. For every smooth datum in the ball, N001 gives the same bound M<=1+A(T,gamma,R). Enlarge constants in N010 using this common bound, so all choices are uniform. For example take N=max(2,ceil(8 C_M)) with C_M>=1, hence choose N>=2 sufficiently large that C_M(N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))<=1/4, then take delta=min(1,1/(4 C_M(N^2+3))) in (0,1] sufficiently small that C_M delta(N^2+3)<=1/4. These exist by the limits of the negative powers and the linear factor in delta. Restrict tau<=delta/2. For intervals starting at grid points with h<=delta, the N010 inequality absorbs its E_I term and gives E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+C_M' delta tau^gamma whenever E_I<=1.

produces.statement: There are uniform N,delta,C_M' depending only on T,gamma,R such that for tau<=delta/2 and |I|<=delta with left grid point and E_I<=1, E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+C_M' delta tau^gamma.

argument.text:
Use successive blocks of \(\lfloor\delta/\tau\rfloor\) steps, whose lengths lie in \([\delta/2,\delta]\), with a possibly shorter final block. The number of blocks is at most \(2T/\delta+1\), independently of \(\tau\). Iterating F001, starting with \(e(0)=0\), yields
\[
\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|e(t)\|_{L^2}\le C_{M,\gamma,T}\tau^\gamma, 
\]
as long as the bootstrap bound is in force. By continuity, if \(\|e\|_{L^2}\) first reached one, the same block argument up to that time would give an upper bound \(C_{M,\gamma,T}\tau^\gamma\). Choosing \(\tau_0\) smaller so that this is less than \(1/2\) gives a contradiction. Hence the accumulated block estimate holds on all of \([0,T]\). The recurrence retains ||e(a)|| on every block and therefore applies when e(a)!=0.
Explicitly set K=ceil(2T/delta)+1 and B_0=0, B_{j+1}=2B_j+C_M' delta. Finite induction gives B_j=C_M' delta(2^j-1). The same bound covers a truncated final block because F001 includes partial last steps. Let C0=max(1,C_M' delta(2^K-1)), and choose tau0=min(1,delta/2,(1/(4 C0))^(1/gamma)), so C0 tau0^gamma<=1/4<1/2; gamma>0 makes this possible. At a hypothetical first hitting time ||e||_2=1, all interval suprema up to and including that time are <=1 by continuity (N001,N007), so the same finite recurrence contradicts C0 tau^gamma<1/2. Thus the bound holds on all [0,T]. At grid points N007 and Airy unitarity give ||e(t_n)||_2=||u(t_n)-u^n||_2. All constants were chosen using the common bound before selecting a datum or a grid.

argument.text: H001,H002 give the original data and exponent conditions. Set u_{0,m}=P_{<=m}u0. Fourier cutoffs preserve reality and zero mean; ||u_{0,m}||_{H^gamma}<=R and ||u_{0,m}-u0||_2->0 by summability of the Fourier norm. N001 gives the common exact-flow bound and sup_{[0,T]}||u_m-u||_2<=C(T,2R)||u_{0,m}-u0||_2->0. N011 applies to every smooth u_{0,m} with the same C0,tau0.

produces.statement: u_{0,m} stay in the original ball, converge to u0 in L2, and sup_t||u_m-u||_2 tends to zero. There exist C0,tau0 depending only on T,gamma,R, the same for all m, such that for tau=T/L<=tau0 every smooth approximating flow and scheme obey max_{0<=n<=L}||u_m(n tau)-u_m^n||_2<=C0 tau^gamma.

argument.text: For each fixed tau>0 the unmodified Psi_tau is continuous L2->L2. N006 gives Dinv:L2->H^1 and the H^1 algebra bound, so F_tau:L2->H^1 is continuous quadratic. The first H_tau term is a product of inverse derivatives, hence continuous. The second uses the bilinear mean P0(f^2), bounded by ||f||_2^2, times S_tau Dinv f. In the third term each endpoint cube (S_s Dinv f)^3 is a continuous H^1 product followed by Dinv. In the fourth, S_{s-tau} Dinv2 F_tau(f) and S_s Dinv f are H^1 factors, followed by Dinv2. All coefficients, including 1/tau, are finite at fixed tau. The Airy terms are continuous by unitarity. Thus every displayed term is continuous into L2, and all iterates are well-defined; their formulas preserve reality and zero mean. For fixed positive L and tau=T/L finite induction gives u_m^n->u^n in L2 at every grid point.

produces.statement: For fixed tau>0, Psi_tau is continuous on L2 and preserves the real mean-zero class. On each fixed finite grid the approximating iterates converge to u^n in L2 at every grid point.

argument.text: Fix any positive L with tau=T/L<=tau0. Using F001,F002 pass to the limit in ||u_m(t_n)-u_m^n||_2<=C0 tau^gamma at every one of its L+1 grid points. Taking their finite maximum gives the output with the same constants. This applies to every datum in the original ball; C0,tau0 were selected using only T,gamma,R. Unitarity identifies physical and twisted errors. No spatial cutoff occurs in Psi; cutoffs appear only in this limiting argument. The solution class and approximation identification are those of N001. This proves the full target.
